title: Carry out basic first aid treatment in the workplace

lessons.title: What to do first in an emergency
lessons.html:
First aid at work

Accidents happen on farms and in stables. A horse can kick, a person can fall, or someone can cut their hand. First aid is the help you give straight away, before a nurse, doctor or ambulance arrives. This lesson gives you basic knowledge. You must also do hands-on training with an accredited first aid provider.

Step 1: Look for danger

  • Is a horse loose? Is a machine still running? Is there fire, electricity or chemicals?
  • Keep yourself safe first. If you get hurt, you cannot help.

Step 2: Check the person

  • Talk loudly: "Can you hear me?" Tap their shoulders.
  • Look if they are breathing: watch the chest go up and down.

Step 3: Call for help

  • Shout for help. Call your supervisor or the first aider.
  • Phone 10177 for an ambulance, or 112 from a cell phone.
  • Say where you are, what happened, and how the person is.
  • Send someone to the farm gate to show the ambulance the way.

Step 4: Protect yourself from blood

Put on gloves from the first aid box before you touch blood. If there are no gloves, use a plastic bag over your hand.

The first aid box

Know where the first aid box is at your work. It has gloves, bandages, plasters, dressings and a triangle bandage. Tell your supervisor when things are used up.

lessons.title: Treating common injuries
lessons.html:
Bleeding

  1. Put on gloves.
  2. Press hard on the wound with a clean dressing or cloth.
  3. Keep pressing. If blood comes through, put another cloth on top. Do not take the first one off.
  4. Tie a bandage firmly over the dressing.
  5. Let the person lie down if they feel weak.

Small cuts and scrapes

Wash with clean water, dry, and cover with a plaster or clean dressing.

Burns

  • Cool the burn under cool running water for at least 20 minutes.
  • Take off rings and watches.
  • Cover with cling wrap or a clean cloth.
  • Never put butter, oil or toothpaste on a burn. Do not burst blisters.

Broken bones

  • Do not move the arm or leg. Keep it still.
  • Support it with soft padding or a sling.
  • Get medical help.

Head or neck injury

If someone fell from a horse and their neck or back hurts, do not move them. Keep the head still. Call for help.

Chemicals in the eye

Wash the eye with lots of clean running water for at least 15 minutes. Take the chemical container label to the clinic.

Fainting

Lay the person down and lift the legs a little. Loosen tight clothes. Give fresh air.

Afterwards

  • Tell your supervisor about every injury, even small ones.
  • The injury must be written in the incident book.
  • Wash your hands with soap.

Key points

  • Check for danger first and keep yourself safe.
  • Phone 10177 or 112 and send someone to the gate.
  • Wear gloves when there is blood.
  • Press hard on a bleeding wound.
  • Cool burns with running water for 20 minutes.
  • Do not move a person with a neck or back injury.
